subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: For ordinary CLI skill publish, should client-declared GitHub source be retained as explicitly unverified attribution, rejected as unsupported, or upgraded only through a new server-verified workflow?
rationale: These directions create materially different trust, storage, API, UI, and compatibility contracts, so implementation cannot safely infer the intended boundary from existing code.

options.title: Separate unverified attribution
options.body: Persist and expose the declared repository, ref, commit, and path under an explicitly unverified field while reserving verify provenance for server-resolved sources.

options.title: Reject unsupported source flags
options.body: Stop accepting source flags for ordinary skill publish and direct publishers to the supported GitHub-backed import path.

options.title: Build verified CLI provenance
options.body: Verify repository access and uploaded content against the claimed commit and path before storing trusted source provenance.

recommendation.title: Separate unverified attribution
recommendation.body: Persist and expose the declared repository, ref, commit, and path under an explicitly unverified field while reserving verify provenance for server-resolved sources.

likelyOwner.reason: The server-resolved GitHub source implementation is the strongest available ownership signal for this trust-contract decision.
